title_en: Tenants have rights: written agreement, rent receipt, basic services
law: Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act, 2017 (Tamil Nadu Act 42 of 2017), Sections 4, 13, 14, 20 and 21
rule_plain: A house can be let on rent only with a written agreement, and the Rent Authority must be told about it. Each time you pay rent, you can ask for a signed written receipt. The landlord must not cut off water, electricity or other basic services, and a tenant cannot be evicted during the agreement except as this law allows, through the Rent Court.
what_you_can_do: Ask your landlord for a written receipt, signed by the landlord or property manager, for every rent payment.
If the landlord will not take your rent or will not give a receipt, send the rent by postal money order for two months in a row. If it is still not accepted, deposit the rent with the Rent Authority.
If water, electricity or another basic service is cut off, complain to the Rent Authority. It can order the service to be restored while it looks into the complaint.
where_to_get_help: The Rent Authority for your area; eviction cases go to the Rent Court.
